changes: Keep per-state frontier reservation counts when budgeting new poses.
Account for existing pending siblings before sharing unused evaluation slots.
Budget root lookahead across selected parents before generation.
Retry only unfilled accepted-candidate targets, independent of previously feasible children.
Reassign slots from exhausted states within the existing retry rounds and widening limits.
Preserve root admission/CEM, serial expansion, fidelity, physical validation and backup accounting.

method.workload: 49 stones total, nine placed; depth three, 512 iterations, seed zero, one search.
method.timing: Fresh sequential processes with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. Search wall excludes setup and teardown.
method.baseline: Existing measurements with the verified pre-change scheduler; not simultaneous timing repeats.
method.profiles: Current CPU/CUDA configurations; 128/128 cases override evaluation batch and native simulation capacity in the benchmark process. Widening-off uses a temporary YAML. Production YAML files unchanged.
method.source_control: Only the common MCTS scheduler differs among recorded Python source hashes; all CUDA comparisons use the identical native binary. The historical CPU reference predates the CUDA-only native rebuild.
method.metrics: For these fresh trees, evaluated_candidates equals tree.evaluated minus the pre-evaluated root; no root retry occurred. Nonfailed rate excludes failures. Parents with evaluated children is a distinct expansion measure computed as tree.evaluated minus frontier_leaves.
limitations: One seed/run per case; this is not a statistical or multi-state speedup claim.
Changed proposal sizes alter RNG consumption and tree allocation; this is not exact search parity.
Current descendant-scoring depth zero makes unchanged selected actions insufficient evidence of equal lookahead quality.
Reducing pending proposals can trade buffered work for smaller batches; report small-batch regressions as well as large-batch gains.
